question: What is SheetSpeed?
answer: A Chrome Manifest V3 extension that adds Excel, Word and PowerPoint Alt shortcuts and key tips to Google Sheets, Docs and Slides. Chrome Web Store ID ljlmgielacploapelnjhodicgbjipcaa. Version referenced in this pack: 0.4.5 (revision 64), repository commit 2e2b338.
evidence: Chrome Web Store; extension repository at main 2e2b338.

question: Do you operate a SaaS backend that stores customer workbooks?
answer: No. Spreadsheet, Doc and Slide content never reaches a SheetSpeed server. Docs processing is local in the browser. Pro tools call Google APIs from the browser after consent.

question: What is the difference between Core and Pro?
answer: Core shortcuts and key tips run on the open Google page and need no Google API access. Pro tools call Google APIs from the browser after the user consents (Sheets; Refresh from Sheets also uses Slides and Drive v3).

question: How is the product distributed and updated?
answer: Only from the Chrome Web Store for production use. Updates are delivered by Google’s Store update mechanism. Do not sideload a zip for a production pilot.

question: Does the extension request <all_urls>?
answer: No. Content scripts are limited to Google Sheets, Docs and Slides document and create URLs.

question: Why is the storage permission required?
answer: To save user settings and a short undo/recovery record in Chrome storage on the profile (and optionally chrome.storage.sync if the user uses Chrome sync).

question: Why is the activeTab permission required?
answer: So a user gesture can act on the tab the user is in, within the documented Google document pages. It is not a blanket right to read every site.

question: Why is the identity permission required?
answer: Chrome Identity is used for Google OAuth when a user starts a Pro tool. The token is Chrome-managed. Dressler Labs does not receive it.

question: Why are Sheets API host permissions required?
answer: So Pro tools can read and write the user’s Google Sheets via sheets.googleapis.com from the browser after consent.

question: Why are Slides and Drive v3 host permissions required?
answer: Refresh from Sheets builds a slide image: it uses slides.googleapis.com and Drive v3 (including upload) to create a temporary PNG. drive.file is not full Drive access.

question: Is nativeMessaging in the Store package?
answer: Not in the early-access Store package. The packaging scripts strip it. Source may still mention a local helper; review the Store package.

question: Is ExtensionPay active during early access?
answer: The early-access Store package drops the ExtensionPay content script. Billing is not open. ExtPay code may still be present in the zip because of a worker import, but it is not constructed while early access is on.

question: Do you load remote code in the extension?
answer: No. The extension CSP includes script-src 'self'.

question: Does the extension include analytics that capture page or spreadsheet content?
answer: No.

question: What data leaves the browser?
answer: Core processing does not leave the device except that the document already lives in Google. Pro API calls go to Google only, from the browser, after consent. Settings may sync via the user’s Chrome profile. Support email the user chooses to send goes to jarvis@agi-jarvis.com. Website visits go to Cloudflare, GitHub Pages, Google Fonts, and Cloudflare Web Analytics. No spreadsheet content is sent to Dressler Labs.
evidence: IT FAQ ‘What leaves the browser’; data map.

question: Where is the Google OAuth token stored?
answer: It is managed by Chrome Identity on the user’s device. Dressler Labs does not receive the token.

question: What is stored in Chrome storage, and for how long?
answer: gridpilotSettings and a short undo/recovery record, for as long as the extension remains installed on that profile (sync follows the user’s Chrome account if enabled). Uninstall deletes extension storage on that profile.

question: Describe the Refresh from Sheets temporary file.
answer: The tool briefly anyone-with-link shares a temporary Drive PNG, then tries to delete it. Cleanup can fail. Leave the tool unused if that is unacceptable. Check Drive for “SheetSpeed refresh (temporary).png”.

question: Do you use customer content to train an AI model?
answer: No. The Store package has no working AI feature and does not send document content to an AI vendor or to Dressler Labs.

question: What personal data does Dressler Labs actually hold?
answer: Support email a person sends, ordinary website analytics identifiers (Cloudflare Web Analytics), and billing identity only after billing opens (ExtensionPay / Stripe). Not workbook content.

question: What is your data-retention practice for support email?
answer: Kept as needed to handle the request and ordinary mailbox practice; deletion can be requested at jarvis@agi-jarvis.com.

question: Is customer workbook data encrypted in transit to you?
answer: Workbook content is not sent to us. Calls to Google APIs use HTTPS from the browser to Google. The website is served over HTTPS.

question: Do you encrypt customer workbooks at rest in your systems?
answer: Not applicable: we do not store customer workbooks. Google and the user’s device hold that data under their controls.

question: How does a customer uninstall and confirm data deletion?
answer: Remove the extension in chrome://extensions if it is not force-installed; an admin must Block or remove Force install if it is. Revoke Google access at myaccount.google.com/permissions. Uninstall deletes Chrome extension storage on that profile. It cannot undo edits already saved in Google files or erase a leftover temporary Drive PNG. Dressler Labs has no copy of workbooks to delete. Ask jarvis@agi-jarvis.com to delete support email.
evidence: IT FAQ: Uninstall and data deletion.

question: What happens on a change of control or shutdown?
answer: There is no published change-of-control clause and no source-code escrow. Intended process: notice on the website and, if still possible, in the extension. Customers can uninstall and revoke Google access at any time. There is no vendor database of workbooks to transfer. This is a residual risk, stated plainly.

question: Cloudflare Web Analytics — is that in use?

question: Can we allowlist, force-install, or block the extension?
answer: Yes, in Google Admin: Devices > Chrome > Apps & extensions > Users & browsers. Allow install, Force install, Block, or Force install + pin to the ChromeOS taskbar. Users cannot remove a force-installed extension. Pilot a small organizational unit first.
evidence: Workspace admin guide; Google support docs 6177431, 6306504, 2657289, 9867568.

question: How do we pin the extension on Windows, Mac, or Linux?
answer: ChromeOS taskbar pin is a Google Admin installation option. For other desktop Chrome, use the ExtensionSettings policy toolbar_pin: force_pinned.

question: How should we treat the OAuth client in API controls?
answer: Use Security > Access and data control > API controls. Prefer “Specific Google data” for the three scopes (spreadsheets, presentations, drive.file), not a blanket Trusted app. The app may be unverified.

question: Does force-install grant the Chrome permissions?
answer: Yes. Removing force-install (or setting Block) removes the extension. OAuth consent for Pro is still a user (or admin-controlled OAuth) step.

question: What is the recommended pilot scope?
